questions.q: What fundamentally distinguishes a dedicated circuit like ExpressRoute or Direct Connect from a site-to-site VPN?
options: A dedicated circuit never touches the public internet, while a VPN tunnel rides over the public internet with IPsec encryption
A dedicated circuit is only usable for accessing public internet services, never private VNets or VPCs
A VPN can only connect two cloud regions, never an on-premises site
Dedicated circuits are provisioned instantly, while VPNs take weeks to months to provision
questions.explain: A dedicated circuit routes traffic entirely over private infrastructure through a connectivity provider's peering location, while a VPN tunnel encrypts traffic that still crosses the public internet.

questions.q: In Azure ExpressRoute, what is the difference between private peering and Microsoft peering?
options: Private peering is for AWS resources; Microsoft peering is for Azure resources
Private peering reaches Azure VNets; Microsoft peering reaches public Microsoft services like Azure Storage or Office 365 without a public internet route
Microsoft peering is required before any VPN Gateway can be created
Private peering only works with ExpressRoute Global Reach enabled
questions.explain: Private peering connects on-premises to Azure VNets, while Microsoft peering connects on-premises to public Microsoft services without the traffic touching the public internet.

questions.q: What problem does an AWS Direct Connect Gateway solve?
options: It encrypts traffic on a Direct Connect connection the way IPsec does for a VPN
It converts a private VIF into a public VIF automatically
It replaces the need for a virtual interface (VIF) entirely
It lets one physical Direct Connect connection serve multiple VPCs or regions instead of requiring a separate connection per VPC
questions.explain: Direct Connect Gateway sits between the physical connection and multiple VPCs, so organizations with more than one VPC or region don't need a separate dedicated connection for each one.

questions.q: Why might a branch office or a dev/test environment use a site-to-site VPN instead of a dedicated circuit?
options: VPNs are the only option that supports IPsec encryption
A dedicated circuit cannot be used for any environment smaller than production
VPNs can typically be stood up in hours once the on-premises router supports IPsec, versus the weeks to months a dedicated circuit's provisioning takes, at lower cost
VPN Gateways provide higher sustained throughput than any ExpressRoute or Direct Connect circuit
questions.explain: VPNs are faster and cheaper to provision than a dedicated circuit, which makes them the right call for sites that need connectivity quickly or don't need the dedicated circuit's throughput and SLA.

questions.q: Why does a standard enterprise pattern configure a VPN as an automatic failover path for an ExpressRoute or Direct Connect circuit?
options: Because a dedicated circuit is not inherently immune to outages, and real resilience comes from having two independent paths rather than one path alone
Because dedicated circuits are not allowed to carry production traffic under any cloud provider's terms of service
Because VPN Gateways have higher bandwidth ceilings than any ExpressRoute or Direct Connect circuit
Because a VPN is required before a dedicated circuit can be provisioned at all
questions.explain: A dedicated circuit can be cut or fail just like any physical link; pairing it with an independent VPN path is what provides actual resilience, with the VPN as reduced-throughput failover rather than the primary path.
